categories.latest: Final Core 0.40 ARM64/x86_64 HAP installed. After cold startup and original network/profile restoration, the actual production system-proxy check returns Google/Gstatic 204 and GitHub 200; this bounded sample does not establish stability. Native network-backup controls verify real authenticated HTTP/SOCKS forwarding on restored ports, missing-auth rejection, bind-conflict rollback, stale previews and original-state recovery. Meaningful runtime, proxy ports/sharing policy, all 11 selections/candidate lists, original backup/profile file lists and exact window placement match the saved user state. categories.limit: Intermittent early external closure remains unresolved. A full independent on-device Shadowsocks AES-GCM reference uses OS cryptography/sockets and the same OS HTTP/1.1 client, pinned to the same endpoint and credentials as the native control. Its 287 public Python/OpenSSL vector assertions pass. Across 12 attempts per site/client, native Google succeeds 10/12 and reference 9/12; Gstatic succeeds 12/12 in both, GitHub 12/12 native and 11/12 reference. Each reference failure closes before receiving any encrypted reply, with no decode/authentication error and no core transfer increments. Thus failure also occurs outside the production core; this does not identify a single cause or prove core correctness. A second existing endpoint completes all 16 Google checks but returns HTTP 403 for all 16 GitHub checks across the two clients, so it was not adopted as a default. These are bounded external samples, not evidence of long-term reliability or full browser compatibility. True-device TUN authorization/background survival and broader protocol interoperability remain unverified.
